title: The Door to the Pass
hook: Hold eastbound. A walker is already in the paint.
scene: Overcast midday daylight on a two-lane downtown street heading east, wet asphalt edge to edge. Flat gray light, no sun, no cast shadows. The Menace is STOPPED short of the stop line, blade CLEAR of the white crosswalk bars — not rolling, no tire spray, not departing east, not inside the markings. The full-width nose plow on the front bull bar points east at a person in a dark coat already on the white bars ahead of the plow. That walker is the hold reason. Brick downtown lines both curbs and continues across and down the far sidewalk so the street does not open onto an empty horizon and is not bunched in one corner. She is not cleared for the pass. Both cats are a sound in the closed carrier on the floor.
debrief: The Beetle is stopped short of the bars. A person is already in the crosswalk. Brick downtown continues across and down the far side of that wet street. She is not cleared for the pass.

source.teaching_target: Hold short of the stop line for a person already in the marked crosswalk; blade clear of the bars; downtown continues on the far side; not in-lane motion; not a rolling-east empty-road departure.

image_brief.camera_pose: Shallower high-oblique aerial, about forty degrees off vertical — off-nadir, not map-flat plan-view, not eye-level, not a steep three-quarter. Same stop/hold geometry as take 36: Beetle STOPPED short of the marked crosswalk, full-width blade CLEAR of the white bars, person already in the paint ahead of the plow, street crossing the frame left to right. Photoreal overcast midday: flat gray-white sky, no sun disk, no cast shadows. Brick downtown continues across the far sidewalk and down that far curb — buildings on both sides of the street, not bunched in one corner, not an empty horizon. The faded pink Beetle is a small mass in the lower half, heading left-to-right, wheels still. NOT a cliffhanger, NOT a rolling-east departure, NOT an empty-road shot.
